chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Minqari from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever drinks the intoxicant and dies while some of it remains in his body, and he has not repented from it, Allah will resurrect him from his grave with his jaw hanging down, his chin tilted, his saliva flowing, calling out with woe and ruin."
ai.seo_question: What is the physical state of resurrection for someone who dies from drinking intoxicants without repenting?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) to detail the specific physical signs of resurrection for those who die in a state of intoxication without repentance. The description of being 'mukhballan' (tilted jaw) and 'sa'il al-lu'ab' (drooling) serves as a literal manifestation of their spiritual disorientation and loss of control during life. This highlights the severity of khamr not merely as a sin, but as a condition that alters one's eternal state in the Hereafter.
